title: Transport fixed-coordinate direct counit to the intrinsic coefficient adjunction
statement: The composite fixed-coordinate counit is the inverse realization of the normalized intrinsic pullback, direct-image comparison, and constant-module adjunction counit.

source.place: Proper-factor paragraph: finite coefficient normalization in the direct counit calculation

proof.text: For the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction, expand its conjugation by the two coefficient equivalences. Naturality of the direct-image comparison and the equivalence unit, followed by the equivalence triangle, give the ordinary counit square.

Derive the ordinary counit square. On a K-injective representative, precompose with the invertible right-derived unit. The published all-complex normalization of the intrinsic direct-image comparison and the canonical cochain counit equation (obtained directly from the source-library derived counit factorization) reduce the result to the ordinary square degree by degree. Naturality extends it to every derived object. Use independent derived Hom universes for the two presentations.

The derived coefficient counit is the levelwise coefficient counit, composed with the prescribed exact-functor composition comparisons. Check its inverse factorization after localization from the homotopy category. The ordinary equivalence identity unit at inverse equals inverse applied to inverse counit proves that the two left comparison maps cancel to the intrinsic pullback applied to the inverse derived counit.

Expand fixedPullRealization and directCoordinates. Transport the exact-derived counit square back through the inverse coefficient equivalence. Naturality cancels the two coefficient units and counits. The K-flat-to-exact pullback comparison transports the exact adjunction to fixedAdjunction. Finally apply naturality to the specified finitePullback and finiteDirectImage realizations.

theorem directCounit_coordinate_transport (S : SixFunctorFiniteOperations D C E n hn)
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (K : sixFunctorFiniteCategory D C E n hn X) :
    letI := Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n hn
    (fixedPullRealization S f ((S.finite.direct f).obj K)).hom ≫
      (fixedDerivedPull (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) f).map
        (directCoordinates S f K).hom ≫
      (fixedAdjunction (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) f).counit.app
        ((coordinates (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) (hn := hn) X).obj K) =
    (realization (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) (hn := hn) X).inverse.map
      ((S.finitePullback f).hom.app ((S.finite.direct f).obj K) ≫
        (sfIntrinsicPullback (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n)
          f.hom.left).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((S.finiteDirectImage f).hom.app K) ≫
        ((sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction f.hom.left
          (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n)).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
          ).counit.app
          ((intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible C.l E n hn X.obj.left).ι.obj K))
